title: Between which two whole numbers does the square root of 250 lie?
description: The square root of two hundred fifty is squeezed between ten and twenty, then between fifteen and sixteen, and the two gaps show which end is nearer. Keeko doubts the nearer end, because the root is less than sixteen.
teaching_notes: One idea: squeeze the root between two squares, then compare the two gaps. Watch for students who say the root is nearer the lower whole number because it is less than the upper one.

source: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does √250 lie, a
video_script.why: The child estimates a square root of a non-square by squeezing it between squares and comparing the two gaps.
video_script.substitution: Find the two squares around the number, then see which one the number is nearer.
video_script.anchor: the number two hundred fifty from the guessing game, written on a card
video_script.wrong_answer: the root is closer to fifteen
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the root is closer to fifteen because it is less than sixteen. Less than sixteen does not mean near fifteen; the gap to two hundred fifty six is only six, but the gap to two hundred twenty five is twenty five.
video_script.payoff_line: The square root of two hundred fifty lies between fifteen and sixteen, closer to sixteen

final_answer.spoken: the square root of two hundred fifty lies between fifteen and sixteen, closer to sixteen

names.Ziva: plays the square root guessing game with the other child
names.Jia: plays the square root guessing game and cannot answer for two hundred fifty

maths_rules: 6 < 25, so √250 is closer to 16, and it is less than 16
video_script.design: One idea: squeeze, then compare the gaps. Wrong idea: less than sixteen means near fifteen. A number line on the stage shows the squares and the gaps.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='game'/>Ziva and Jia play a game. One says a number, and the other replies with its square root.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Ziva says twenty five, and Jia replies five. Then Jia says eighty one, and Ziva answers nine.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Next, Ziva says two hundred fifty. Jia cannot answer, because it is not a perfect square.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which two whole numbers does its square root lie between, and which is it closer to?

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the two whole numbers its square root lies between, and which one is nearer.

marks.between: 100 < 250 < 400 is written and the root is marked between 10 and 20

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step one, use the squares of ten and twenty.
Ten squared is one hundred, and twenty squared is four hundred.
<bookmark mark='between'/>Two hundred fifty sits between them, so the root is between ten and twenty.

marks.squeeze: 225 < 250 < 256 is written and the root is marked between 15 and 16

narration: <bookmark mark='near'/>Step two, squeeze it tighter.
Fifteen squared is two hundred twenty five, and sixteen squared is two hundred fifty six.
<bookmark mark='squeeze'/>Two hundred fifty sits between them, so the root is between fifteen and sixteen.

beats.on_screen: gaps: 256 − 250 = 6 and 250 − 225 = 25; the smaller gap is 6

narration: <bookmark mark='up'/>Step three, compare the two gaps.
Two hundred fifty six minus two hundred fifty is six.
<bookmark mark='down'/>Two hundred fifty minus two hundred twenty five is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The smaller gap is six, on the side of two hundred fifty six.

beats.on_screen: Answer: √250 lies between 15 and 16, closer to 16

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The square root of two hundred fifty lies between fifteen and sixteen, closer to sixteen.
It is still a little less than sixteen.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the root is closer to fifteen, because it is less than sixteen.
<bookmark mark='gaps'/>But less than sixteen does not mean near fifteen. The gap to sixteen squared is only six, and the gap to fifteen squared is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Only the smaller gap tells us which end is nearer.
